items.title: Senate Panel Holds Fauci in Contempt of Congress
items.author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
items.content: <article>Dr. Anthony Fauci had refused to answer questions at a hearing last week, invoking the Fifth Amendment. Republicans argued that he wasn’t entitled to that protection because he had a presidential pardon.</article>

items.title: Senate Panel Votes to Hold Fauci in Contempt
items.author: Jan Hoffman
items.content: <article>The case is unique, legal scholars say, because of the tension between the Fifth Amendment and the reach of a presidential pardon. The potential consequences could be grave.</article>

items.title: Trump Made Calls to Warsh in Latest Sign of Bid to Influence Fed
items.author: Josh Wingrove and Enda Curran
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump has periodically spoken by phone with Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh since he took the role, people familiar with the matter said, the latest sign of Trump’s effort to exert greater influence over the central bank.</article>

items.title: Lithuania Sees Russia Mulling False-Flag Drone Attack on Region
items.author: Milda Seputyte
items.content: <article>Lithuania said Russia is weighing a potential false flag operation using captured Ukrainian drones to strike critical infrastructure in the Baltic region.</article>

items.title: US Says Oklo’s Small Nuclear Reactor Reaches ‘Criticality’
items.author: Ari Natter
items.content: <article>Oklo Inc.’s small modular reactor has reached a key milestone, the Energy Department announced Thursday.</article>

items.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
items.author: Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate, with unabashedly liberal positions, win a general election in a moderate state?</article>

items.title: Xi Flexes Expanding Legal Arsenal to Warn Trump Ahead of Summit
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s latest barrage of countermeasures against the US drew on an expanding legal arsenal, demonstrating Beijing’s growing capacity to retaliate while warning Washington against further tech curbs before Xi Jinping’s expected visit next month.</article>

items.title: Virginia Governor to Intervene in NextEra-Dominion Merger
items.author: Emily Forgash
items.content: <article>Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger said she’ll intervene in her state’s review of NextEra Energy Inc.’s $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc. over concerns about the deal’s impact of electricity affordability.</article>

items.title: Iceland’s Pro and Anti-EU Camps Tie in Poll Ahead of Referendum
items.author: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir
items.content: <article>Iceland is set for a close result in a referendum on resuming talks with the European Union later this month, according to the latest poll.</article>

items.title: Democrats Enter Fundraising Blitz While Bashing Corporate Cash
items.author: Kate Ackley
items.content: <article>The split-screen is likely to continue through November and into the next Congress.</article>

items.title: US Asks Manila to Extradite Duterte-Allied Pastor Quiboloy Wanted by FBI
items.author: Cliff Venzon
items.content: <article>The US has asked the Philippines to extradite a Filipino evangelical preacher wanted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation for alleged sex trafficking, risking further political tensions in the Southeast Asian nation.</article>

items.title: India’s Student Movement Shuns Politics, Stays Pressure Group
items.author: Akriti Sharma
items.content: <article>The Cockroach Janta Party, which spearheaded India’s biggest student protests in recent years, said it won’t become a political party, opting instead to remain a “pressure group” after weeks of demonstrations forced Prime Minister Narendra Modi to replace his education minister.</article>

items.title: Ceuta and Michigan Expose Political Fault Lines Playing Out in Germany
items.author: Alan Crawford
items.content: <article>Polls for three German state elections next month show the tussle between progressive politics and anti-migrant sentiment.</article>

items.title: Iran Says Deal With Oman on Hormuz Agreed in Principle
items.author: Eltaf Najafizada
items.content: <article>The wait for an Iran-Oman deal that partially reopens the Strait of Hormuz continued into Thursday, after the Islamic Republic said an agreement on proposed shipping lanes was in the final stages.</article>

items.title: Tennessee’s Andy Ogles Faces Well-Funded Opposition in House Primary Thursday
items.author: Patricia Mazzei, Tim Balk and Emily Cochrane
items.content: <article>Representative Andy Ogles received President Trump’s endorsement, but his challenger, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, has the backing of Gov. Bill Lee.</article>

items.title: Sheinbaum’s Approval Jumps as Inflation Cools to Five-Year Low
items.author: Gonzalo Soto
items.content: <article>Mexico President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval rating jumped in July as inflation slowed and economic expectations improved.</article>

items.title: Ukraine Says It Hit Two of Russia’s Oil Refineries Overnight
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Ukraine struck two of Russia’s oil refineries overnight, the latest in a flurry of attacks that signal a resumption of the assault on the nation’s fuel-producing industry.</article>

items.title: North Korea Fires Missile After Warning of Military Steps
items.author: Soo-Hyang Choi
items.content: <article>North Korea fired a short-range ballistic missile off its east coast Thursday, South Korea’s military said, a day after Pyongyang warned of fresh military steps over Japan’s expanding defense capabilities.</article>

items.title: Commerzbank Says Teaming Up With UniCredit Could Be Positive | Daybreak Europe 8/6/2026
items.content:
<article>Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. 

On today's show, Commerzbank says a strategy developed together with UniCredit could be beneficial for investors, extending an olive branch to the Italian rival that’s set to take control of it. The comments came as the German lender announced a €1.2 billion share buyback, after second quarter net income beat estimates.

Siemens has raised its earnings expectations for a second time this year on a surge in data center spending and higher returns from selling software to industry.

Global stocks slipped from record highs, as disappointing guidance from US memory makers Sandisk and Western Digital weighed on sentiment.

And Iran says it has reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.

Today's guest: Bettina Orlopp, Commerzbank CEO & Roland Busch, Siemens CEO (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Denies US Munitions Shortage, Warns ‘Leakers’ of Jail Time
items.author: Ryan Chua
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump denied the US was running low on munitions, saying the country has “massive amounts” of them, while warning of punishment for those who say there’s a shortage.</article>

items.title: Thailand Welcomes Myanmar Leader in Push to End Isolation
items.author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat and Khine Lin Kyaw
items.content: <article>Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul welcomed Myanmar’s former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing on his first visit to Thailand since becoming a civilian leader, underscoring Bangkok’s push to rebuild its neighbor’s ties with other Southeast Asian nations.</article>

items.title: Burnham’s High-Speed Train Dream Hinges on a Fiscal Revolution
items.author: Jacob Reid

items.title: Bangladesh ‘Outraged’ With India Over Ex-Leader’s Media Briefing
items.author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen

items.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
items.author: Christina Jewett

items.title: José Antonio Kast Kast Unveils Tougher Agenda to Fight Organized Crime
items.author: Antonia Mufarech

items.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
items.author: Adam Entous
items.content: <article>The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.</article>

items.title: After Michigan Loss, AIPAC Weighs a Second Effort to Defeat El-Sayed
items.author: Jennifer Medina and Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>The pro-Israel organization spent $32 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It might try again in the general election.</article>

items.content: <article>The National Firearms Act mandated a permitting process for short-barreled rifles and shotguns, as well as suppressors. A judge ruled that the provision was unconstitutional.</article>

items.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
